title: Does the sorted Schmidt basis minimize nonlocal magic?
locator: Sierant, Conjecture 1, equations 3–6. Open Quantum Problems E27.
question: For every bipartite pure state of qubits, does the sorted computational-basis Schmidt representative minimize the stabilizer 2-Rényi entropy over independent local unitaries?
significance: An exact answer would turn an optimization over all local bases into an evaluation on the entanglement spectrum.
known: The working paper covers all rank-seven spectra for three qubits per party, three open regions of the larger-register problem and spectra with two exceptional amplitudes in equal registers. Independent project review is available.
experiment: Test the unresolved pair-frame inequality outside spans containing a stabilizer direction. An exact violation would identify the limit of this proof route.
full_vs_partial: Arbitrary rank and local register sizes are required for the full conjecture. A strictly lower entropy for a state on the same local-unitary orbit would refute it.
stop_rule: For larger registers, test the five outstanding coefficient inequalities against physical frames before extending the theorem.

title: First priority · A 43-gate Golay preparation
locator: Ganesan, Appendix A.4, explicit 43-gate challenge; Open Quantum Problems A50
question: Can the logical zero of the 23-qubit quantum Golay code be prepared with at most 43 CNOT gates, on exactly 23 qubits, with free single-qubit Clifford gates, no measurements and no ancillas?
significance: Direct reduction of the two-qubit gate cost of preparing an error-correcting code state. The full depth/count frontier is a larger question.
known: 44 entanglers in six layers is an explicit deposited circuit. The originating agent already tried 43 and reported an unsuccessful 92-million-neighbor delete-two/insert-one screen.
experiment: Reverse a trial 43-gate schedule on the exact target stabilizer. Start with systematic changes to the public 44-gate seed, then search different axes, wire pairs and orders.
full_vs_partial: One explicitly reconstructed circuit with a signed-stabilizer verification in cyclic coordinates answers yes. A no requires a lower bound over all allowed circuits. Failed local searches establish neither a lower bound nor optimality.
stop_rule: Run eight bounded reproducible batches or stop immediately for an independently verified candidate; on a plateau switch search family before increasing the budget.

title: Exact approximation of quantum transport costs
locator: Pitchford, Conjecture 7.7 and Proposition 7.5, release v0.1.0-candidate
question: For 0 < p ≤ 1 < q, is the polygon bound exact for every finite spectrum and attained by a single exponent-one function of the observable?
significance: Computes the optimal operator-norm error for approximating one quantum transport cost by lower-exponent observables.
known: Project proof and separate project-agent mathematical review cover every finite spectrum in the registered range. External review is pending.
experiment: Enumerate every polygon chain for integer spectra and exponents, then solve the difference constraints exactly. Save labels; verify each pair. Audit every ordering for a small obstruction.
full_vs_partial: A proof for all finite spectra or one certified counterexample to either prediction settles the stated conjunction. A failed monotone fit alone is insufficient. A strict distance failure requires a bound against the full cut cone.
stop_rule: Rotate away after eight unchanged batches of integer spectra. Keep attained instances as evidence, without discovery credit.

locator: Open Quantum Problems, Problem 2; distillability criterion and Werner reduction
question: Does there exist a bipartite state with negative partial transpose from which no entanglement can be distilled using any finite number of copies?
significance: Separates two fundamental notions of usable entanglement. Answering it requires reasoning about all copy counts or all candidate states.
known: The three-copy endpoint has a reported proof. Four-copy results cover same-plane range and co-range, including normal rank-two matrices. The cited project reports additional Hermitian results. Check its current version before promoting a witness.
experiment: Qutrit endpoint, four and five copies. Seek a negative expectation on a complex vector with Schmidt rank at most two; enforce both exact contractions.
full_vs_partial: A strict negative witness would settle distillability of the specified state at that copy count. The overarching existential question would remain open. Nonnegative samples and coordinate-support classifications leave even the finite-copy target unresolved.
stop_rule: After three unchanged rounds for both objectives, reduce sampling and give the other sourced problem the primary slot. Periodically retry the Werner arm.

locator: Gagatsos, Conjecture 1, Eq. (7), with the conventions in Eqs. (2)-(5)
question: For every single-mode state, is the Wigner L1 norm at most the squared integral of sqrt(Q) divided by 8 pi, with equality exactly for coherent states?
significance: The conjectured sharp bound would connect heterodyne statistics to Wigner negativity and the sampling overhead of quasiprobability simulation. The statement is recent; its long-term standing is unknown.
known: The source gives pure-state reduction, a factor-two bound, finite Fock numerical experiments, and a cat construction against higher Renyi orders. Wigner-positive states follow from Lieb–Solovej. A bounded title/author and modulation-space/STFT search found no subsequent sharp resolution. Priority is provisional.
restricted_result: The phase-invariant case, for every photon-number distribution, has a written proof in papers/phase-invariant-wigner.tex. Its arithmetic induction step is checked in formal/FockMoment.lean. The zero–one-photon subspace now also has a separate analytic proof. Sec. VII question (iv) has new order exclusions and an exact threshold on the full optical qubit. The sparse-state note rules out all states of coherence number at most two within levels zero through five. Current search tests higher photon pairs and genuinely three-level states. See checks/phase-invariant-wigner.md and checks/optical-sprint.md.
experiment: Optimize squeeze, weight, separation and phase of a normalized pure two-coherent-state superposition. Use two refined grids and analytic positive/negative-Wigner controls.
full_vs_partial: A single state with a rigorously positive residual would refute the universal inequality. Floating point can nominate it; original normalization, explicit quadrature error and tail bounds must then be verified. No violation in a family gives no proof of the universal statement.
stop_rule: A positive refined residual is queued for error-bounded validation. Without a crossing, record the family, parameters and residual and retain proof status as open.

title: A lower bound for symmetrized quantum partition functions
locator: IQOQI problem 40, lower bound. Hägele, arXiv:2611.00129v1, Eq. (1) and Lemmas 2, 5 and 6.
question: For all finite-dimensional Hermitian H,K and positive integers n,m, is the mean trace of words with n factors exp(H) and m factors exp(K) at least Tr exp(nH+mK)?
significance: This would bound a quantum partition function using symmetrized products of two noncommuting positive matrices.
known: The all-degree three-second-factor theorem for up to three first-matrix eigenvalues is already public. We independently reproduced 26 of its cases. The binary-spectrum coefficient argument covers both bounds and arbitrary word counts.
experiment: For three spectral values and at least four factors of the second matrix, analyze the histogram weights in the trace of a three-variable matrix pencil. Identify which signed coefficients can survive the weighted sum in the lower bound.
full_vs_partial: The catalogue lower bound quantifies over all finite dimensions and both word counts. A proof in dimension three with three second factors is partial.
stop_rule: Promote only an explicit all-input certificate or a rigorously verified violating matrix pair. Keep finite word-count sweeps grouped in one result.

title: Optimal check weight for twelve physical qubits encoding three
locator: Wei et al., Table 2, distance-four row n=12, k=3 (6–8); binary stabilizer codes.
question: What is the minimum possible maximum generator weight of a binary [[12,3,4]] stabilizer code, over all codes and generating sets?
significance: Measures the lightest possible largest parity check while encoding three logical qubits and detecting every Pauli error of weight up to three.
known: Wei et al. report 6–8. Jing and Tu retained that interval in their distance-four table.
experiment: Generate bounded-weight commuting checks, fix one logical Pauli of known parent codes, and challenge the universal lower bound by exact weight-enumerator constraints.
full_vs_partial: An independent rank-nine commuting basis of maximum weight six with exact distance four attains six. The quantum weight-enumerator constraints and two exact rational dual identities exclude nine weight-at-most-five stabilizers in any eligible code, including degenerate groups.
stop_rule: Release only after independent review of the source, both bounds and priority.

title: Optimal check weight for twelve physical qubits encoding four
locator: Wei et al., Table 2, distance-four row n=12, k=4 (7–8); binary stabilizer codes.
question: What is the minimum possible maximum generator weight of a binary [[12,4,4]] stabilizer code, over all codes and generating sets?
significance: A distance-four code storing four logical qubits achieves seven-qubit parity checks, fewer than the eight used by the tabulated construction.
known: The two compared tables retain the interval 7–8. The archived Grassl code needs weight eight in any basis.
experiment: Keep seven independent checks of the Grassl group and replace its eighth. Check distance and the minimum generating weight of each new group.
full_vs_partial: An independent rank-eight commuting basis of maximum weight seven with exact distance four attains seven. Two rational dual identities bound the number of stabilizers with support at most six by six or two according to parity, covering degenerate codes as well.
stop_rule: Release only after independent review of the source, both bounds and priority.

title: Optimal check weight for ten qubits encoding two
locator: Wei et al., Table 2, n=10, k=2, d=4 (5–6).
question: What is the minimum possible maximum generator weight of a binary [[10,2,4]] stabilizer code, over all codes and generating sets?
significance: Determines how light the checks can be for a ten-qubit, two-logical-qubit, distance-four binary stabilizer.
known: Grassl’s code attains six. Wei et al. left five possible. Zhang resolved different lengths eleven and twelve.
experiment: Extend each candidate to a self-dual graph-state parent. Enumerate all subgroups and check light stabilizers after imposing the distance criterion.
full_vs_partial: The Grassl code attains six. Over every graph-state parent from the Danielsen–Parker classification including disconnected products, the distance-compatible rank-eight subspaces have no nonidentity stabilizers of weight at most five. Every eligible group extends to a graph-state parent up to weight-preserving equivalence.
stop_rule: Release only after independent review of the source, both bounds and priority.
